text.content:
This is a complete evening of Don’t Get Forked for 3–5 players who have never played. It teaches the game as it goes, so nobody needs to read the rulebook first, not even you. Read this page and the next before your guests arrive; everything after that you can read aloud at the table.

From the Designer

This is not a game where the Storyteller is trying to beat the players. You are creating room for chaos and letting the chaos take the table in various directions that will result in fun outcomes. The players dying is the fate of the dice, not the objective for running the game.

Richard Moore

How to Read This Script

  • Boxes marked “Read aloud” are for the players. Read them word for word.
  • Gray, smaller text is for you alone. It tells you what to ask, what to roll and what to write down.
  • The Places has a page for every place in town. When the party goes somewhere, turn to that page.
  • When It Happens has a box for everything the dice can do, from a Cost or Trouble to a chase, a capture, a Tell or the final flight. When one of these happens, turn to its box and read it.
  • The rules here are the rulebook’s, written in plain words, so the book agrees with them. If a question comes up that this script doesn’t answer, make a quick ruling and keep the game moving.

What You Need

  • Each player: one each of d4, d6, d8, d10 and d12, plus a second d6 (the Mask) and a second d10 (the Monster), each in a different color from the trait dice. A 0 on a d10 counts as 10. Players can share if you’re short.
  • You: a d6 (for Tells and chases) and this script.
  • The Entity cards, one per Entity, from The Eight Entities near the end. The rulebook’s defaults are already chosen. Print the cards and cut them out so the players can choose. The Castle Duty can be changed at the table (Part One).
  • The tracker on the last page, printed out. It keeps track of Suspicion, the Turns, the Lead, the shopping list and the lock-up, with a coin or a token on each track.
  • The map of Hallowby (Hallowby at a Glance). Print that page a second time, larger if you can, and put it where everyone can see it. Players move a token or a coin to show where their Entity is.

The Evening at a Glance

20–25 minPart One: The Castle. Who the players are, the shopping list, choosing Entities and Castle Duties, and a practice roll.
45–90 minPart Two: Into Hallowby. The raid: twelve Turns of sneaking, rolling and maybe running.
0–15 minThe final flight, if the town turns out with pitchforks.
5–10 minPart Three: How the Year Went. What came home, and how the castle’s year goes.

If your group wants a break, take it after Part One, right before the raid.

The Night in Numbers

Hallowby is an Easy town. Keep these numbers handy; they’re on the tracker too.

  • The shopping list: 4 items. One is essential, the cask of red wine.
  • Turns: 12, then dawn. Charges: 3 for each Entity.
  • Suspicion: starts at 0. The Limit is 9, or 8 with five players. When Suspicion reaches it, the whole town hunts the party in the final flight.
  • The way out: Difficulty 6. The lock-up: Difficulty 10.
  • A local chase: the Lead starts at 1, escape at 4, against a mob of 8 plus half the Suspicion when the chase starts (rounded down, at most 11). The chase raises Suspicion once, when it ends. It lasts 6 rounds at most.
  • The final flight: the Lead starts at 2, escape at 5, against a mob of 10.

Running a Turn

The raid is twelve Turns. Run each Turn like this (it’s on the tracker too).

  1. Say the Turn, as in “Turn 3.” The marker moves at the end of each Turn, in step 5.
  2. Go around the table. Ask each player, “What does your Entity do?” Each takes one action, which is to roll at the next obstacle where it is, move to another place, pick up dropped items, or wait. They act one at a time, in any order they like, and each result counts at once.
  3. A move takes the Turn, and the Entity is there now. Turn to that place’s page and read its arrival box. If it’s a watched place that nobody has reached yet (for the way out, the first time anyone comes back to it; at the lock-up, a captive’s arrival doesn’t count), make a Tell check once everyone moving there this Turn has arrived. If you’re not sure who else is coming, ask before the next roll (When It Happens).
  4. A roll. Ask which trait, Mask or Monster, and whether anyone spends a charge. Then they roll, you read the result and you mark any Suspicion. One roll raises Suspicion once, by its biggest trigger (an overdraw adds its +2 on top).
  5. End of the Turn. If the mirror has been taken and is still in town, Suspicion +1. Then move the Turn marker. If that was Turn 12, dawn comes (When It Happens).

Whenever Suspicion reaches the Limit, finish the roll’s result first, then stop wherever you are and turn to The Final Flight. If that roll got the party out of town, they’re out and nobody runs. If it got someone caught, there’s no local chase, and they run in the final flight with everyone else.

Keeping it moving

  • Let the players plan out loud, but if a Turn stalls, ask the quietest player what they do.
  • The party can split up. Hallowby is small enough to go around together, but splitting up saves Turns.
  • When a player asks “Can I…?”, the answer is usually “Yes, if you get past the obstacle,” and they can try any trait if they say how (Other ideas, The Places). Every place is in this script, and nothing else needs a roll.
  • Anyone with nothing to do, such as a player waiting at the bridge or in the lock-up, can play a villager, like Granny Mott, the constable or a costume contest judge.
  • Give the villagers voices and keep the rules talk short. The script keeps track of the rules so you don’t have to.

Easy. A small market town where everyone turns out for Lantern Night.

Lantern Night: Turnip lanterns in every window.

The shopping list (4 items):

  1. A cask of red wine (essential)
  2. A pot of nightshade
  3. A set of new hinges
  4. A new cape

The furniture: a gold-framed mirror (Bulky: one carrier), at the tailor (4).

Villagers: old Granny Mott, who has seen it all before (carrying a lantern and a pitchfork for the parade); a gang of children (judging the costume contest).

Easy: Suspicion Limit 9 (8 with five players) · Difficulty: the way out 6, the lock-up 10 · the final flight: mob 10, Lead 2, escape at 5.

Location · obstacleQuiet wayLoud wayDifficulty
1. The tavern cellar: a cask of red wine (food and drink) · essential

or A heavy cellar trapdoorBrawn—8

Way in A crowded shop (group) watchedSly—8
or A rickety drainpipeNimble—10

Way in A locked front door watchedSly (pick the lock)Brawn (kick it in)8
or A high garden wallNimbleBrawn (break through the gate)8

Reading the key. Each location’s rows run in order: its two ways in (the party picks one the first time anyone tries the location, then keeps it for the night), then each “Then”. Watched: Trouble there gets you caught. (group): each Entity rolls for itself. The loud way works too, at Suspicion +1 whatever the result. The guard dog’s Difficulty is already 2 harder: it guards the furniture. On the map, an eye marks a watched location and the star marks the mirror. Every move takes one Turn (two carrying the mirror).

About 20–25 minutes. Have the Entity cards face up in the middle of the table, the map of Hallowby where everyone can see it, and the tracker beside you, set to Suspicion 0 and Turn 1. When everyone is settled, begin.

Welcome

Tonight is Halloween, and you’re playing monsters, the real kind.

You all live together in an old castle in the woods above a small town called Hallowby. The castle is out of almost everything it needs, and the only way to restock is to take it from the town.

Once a year, Hallowby holds a festival called Lantern Night. Everyone in town wears a costume and carries a lantern through the streets until sunrise. It’s the one night a real monster can walk through town without anyone looking twice.

You have until sunrise to steal everything on the castle’s shopping list and bring it home. If the town gets too suspicious, everyone comes after you with pitchforks and you have to run for the castle. If they catch you, you get forked.

The Shopping List

Point to the four places on the map as you read each item.

The castle’s shopping list is pinned to the kitchen door. There are four things on it.

  • A cask of red wine, from the cellar of the tavern. This one is essential, because without it the castle can’t have a good year.
  • A pot of nightshade, from the florist.
  • A set of new hinges, from the carpenter.
  • A new cape, from the tailor.

At the bottom, someone has added, “A mirror would be nice too.”

If you bring home the wine and miss no more than one of the other three, that’s a good year, a Win. If you do all that and also bring home a piece of furniture, it’s a Grand Year. There’s a gold-framed mirror at the tailor’s.

Choosing Your Monster

Read the eight introductions, pointing to each card. Then let the players choose.

Eight monsters live in the castle. Each of you plays one, and no two of you can play the same one.

  • Dracula is the best talker in the castle. He can look a guard in the eye and walk right past, but he can’t stand garlic.
  • Frankenstein’s Creature is the strongest. It breaks the locks others would pick, and it carries furniture better than anyone.
  • The Mummy is the smartest. It’s three thousand years old and remembers every trick there is.
  • The Werewolf is the fastest. When the wolf shows, the crowd just sees a very large dog.
  • The Invisible Man is the sneakiest. Nobody can catch what they can’t see, unless he’s carrying something.
  • A Ghost drifts through walls and slips past crowds, but it can’t stand cold iron.
  • A Witch is a good friend to have nearby, because her spell can make anyone’s roll better. Her black cat warns her when someone is watching.
  • Jekyll & Hyde is two monsters in one body. One is a kind doctor, and the other is a brute who comes out at the worst times.

Each of you, pick one and take its card.

If two players want the same Entity, they roll off (again on a tie): the high d6 keeps it, and the other chooses again. Once everyone has a card, ask each player in turn to say their Entity’s name, so everyone knows who’s who. If asked: the Werewolf’s very large dog costs a charge. Tonight’s mirror is Bulky, so anyone can carry it, and the Creature’s Tireless means carrying it doesn’t make its Nimble smaller.

Your Card

Look at your card. Every monster has five traits: Brawn for force and lifting, Nimble for climbing and running, Sly for sneaking and stealing, Charm for talking and passing as human, and Wits for noticing things and figuring them out.

Each trait is a die. You all have the same five dice, a d4, d6, d8, d10 and d12, in a different order. Your d12 is what you’re best at, and your d4 is what you’d rather leave to someone else.

Every time you roll, you add a second die, and you choose which one. If you pick the Mask, a d6, you keep your costume on and pass as human. If you pick the Monster, a d10, you let the monster out. The Monster is stronger, but if its number comes up higher than your trait die’s, the town sees what you really are. That raises Suspicion, the whole town’s alarm, by 2.

Suspicion is one track that you all share. When it reaches 9 (8 if there are five of you), the whole town comes after you, so try to keep it low.

A Practice Roll

Nothing in this practice counts. There’s no Suspicion and no charges, and Jekyll stays Jekyll. Ask each player to roll their d12 trait with the Mask d6, add them, and tell you the total. Read the box as far as the Critical, tell each player their result, then read its last paragraph.

Every roll is against a number called the Difficulty, which is a 6, 8, 10 or 12. The bigger it is, the harder the roll. For this one, let’s say it’s 8.

  • 8 or more is a Success. You do it.
  • 1 or 2 short, a 6 or a 7, is a Cost. You still do it, but something goes wrong, and I pick what it is.
  • 3 or more short is Trouble. You don’t do it, and Suspicion goes up. If someone was watching, you’re caught and you have to run.
  • And if both dice show the same number on a Success, that’s a Critical, and something extra good happens.

Now roll the d12 again, this time with the Monster d10 instead of the Mask. If the d10 came up higher than the d12, the Monster showed. The Monster usually helps you succeed, but every time it shows tonight, Suspicion goes up by 2. The Mask never shows.

When everyone has rolled, go on.

Your Powers

Each of you has 3 charges. One charge pays for one use of an ability, either your Signature or your Gift, and both are on your card. Spend the charge before you roll. An ability never gets you past an obstacle on its own; you still have to roll.

Almost every ability does one of four things: it makes your trait die one size bigger, lets you roll a different trait, lets you roll the Monster without raising Suspicion, or opens a way past an obstacle that only you can take. Your card says which. Jekyll’s Draught is the one exception, because it changes his form. And when the town is chasing you, any ability can make your trait die one size bigger instead.

You can also spend a charge on a friend’s roll if you’re in the same place. It uses your charge but not your action. Only one thing can make a die bigger on any one roll, and if something also makes it smaller, the two cancel out.

If you run out of charges, you can still use an ability. That’s called an overdraw, and instead of a charge it costs Suspicion +2, on top of anything else the roll raises.

Your Perk is always on, and it’s free. Your Weakness is something the mob brings along when it chases you, and your Tell is the small thing that gives you away. Tonight, keep the Gift and Perk on your card.

Castle Duties

One last thing. Everyone at the castle has a job, called a Castle Duty, and does the shopping for it. At the place where your Duty’s item is, your trait die is one size bigger on your own rolls.

Tonight’s list needs a Cook for the wine, a Gardener for the nightshade, a Handyman for the hinges and a Tailor for the cape. The Butler and the Librarian have nothing to buy tonight.

Your card already has a Duty. You can keep it or switch to any Duty nobody else has, but no two of you can have the same one.

If two players want the same Duty, they roll off (again on a tie): the high d6 keeps it, and the other picks another. Write each player’s Duty on the tracker. The six Duties are Cook, Gardener, Librarian, Butler, Handyman and Tailor.

Setting Off

The castle door creaks open. Down the hill, through the trees, you can see Hallowby glowing. There’s a turnip lantern in every window, and music is coming from the square.

You check your costumes one last time and start down the path to town.

Turn to Part Two.

About 45–90 minutes, plus the final flight if it comes. Read the next two boxes, then start Turn 1.

The Edge of Town

The path comes out of the woods at the bottom of the hill, next to a small stone bridge. That bridge is your way out, and when it’s time to go home, you all meet back here.

On the other side, the festival is in full swing. Carved turnips glow in every window, and a fiddle band is playing in the square. Children dressed as bats chase children dressed as ghosts. An old woman carrying a lantern and a pitchfork for the parade gives you a long look, then decides you’re just people in costume.

How the Night Works

The night lasts 12 Turns. When the twelfth is over, the sun comes up.

Each Turn, each of you does one thing. You can roll to get past something, move to another place, pick up something that was dropped, or wait. You go one at a time, in any order you like, and everything happens right away. You can split up if you want.

Moving anywhere on the map takes one Turn. The places are the four on the list, the lock-up and the bridge.

Every place on the list has obstacles, like a locked door or a nosy shopkeeper. You get past them in order, and whoever gets past the last one has the item. Each obstacle tells you which traits work and how hard it is, but you can try other ideas too.

Every place on the list has two ways in. The first time any of you tries a place, you choose one, and that’s your way in there for the rest of the night.

Once one of you gets past an obstacle, it stays beaten for everybody, with two exceptions. Everyone gets past a crowd for themselves, and a way that only you can take (your card says when) is beaten only for you.

Some obstacles have a loud way. It works, but it puts Suspicion up by 1, whatever you roll.

Some obstacles are watched. If you get Trouble at a watched one, you’re caught, and you have to run for it. If the crowd corners you, you go to the lock-up, and the others can get you out.

The first time any of you reaches a watched place (the bridge counts when you come back to it), I roll a die to see whether a Tell gives you away. That’s Suspicion +1.

You can hand things to each other any time you’re in the same place, and you can carry as much as you like. The mirror is the exception, because it’s furniture, and furniture is heavy.

When you’re done, everyone not locked up meets at the bridge, and one of you rolls to get you all out of town.

And keep an eye on Suspicion. If it reaches 9 (8 if there are five of you), or you’re still in town when the sun comes up, the whole town hunts you, and you all run for the castle together. That’s the final flight, and it’s how monsters get forked.

Then begin.

It’s Turn 1. Where do you go?

If they can’t decide, the tavern cellar is an easy first stop, since nothing there is watched and it has the essential. Turn to The Places for wherever they go.

Your first roll: walk them through it

  1. The first time anyone tries a place, ask “Which way in?” Read both, and they choose.
  2. “Which trait?” Read them the obstacle’s choices; for other ideas, see the start of The Places.
  3. “Mask or Monster?”
  4. “Is anyone spending a charge?” Ask before the roll. The charge can be theirs or a friend’s at the same place.
  5. Castle Duty. If this place has the item for the roller’s Duty, their trait die is one size bigger (a d8 becomes a d10; a d12 stays a d12). That’s the roll’s one bigger die, so no ability can add another.
  6. Bigger and smaller. If something also makes the die smaller (a Cost, a Weakness, carrying the mirror unless you’re the Creature), cancel them one for one first, so a d12 made bigger and smaller stays a d12. Then no die goes below a d4 or above a d12.
  7. Roll and add, and compare with the Difficulty to see if it’s a Success, a Cost (1–2 short) or Trouble (3 or more short). Doubles on a Success make a Critical.
  8. Suspicion. The loud way +1, Trouble +1, the Monster shows +2. One roll raises it once, by its biggest, so the loud way and the Monster showing make +2, not +3. An overdraw is the exception: its +2 goes on top.
  9. Read the result’s line from the obstacle. For a Cost or Trouble, turn to When It Happens.

What Raises Suspicion

Trouble+1
The Monster shows+2
Taking the loud way+1, whatever the result
A Cost picked as Suspicion+1
Overdraw+2, on top of the roll’s other rise
A Tell goes off+1 (not from a roll)
The mirror, once taken+1 at the end of every Turn, even set down, until it leaves town, is lost or is abandoned

One roll raises Suspicion only once, by its biggest trigger, and an overdraw adds +2 on top. A local chase raises it once, when the chase ends. Good results never lower it. It never goes past the Limit, and reaching it starts the final flight at once.

One page for each place on the map. When anyone arrives, read the arrival box. The first time anyone tries a location, read both ways in and let them choose (getting in by a way a power opens counts as choosing too). The party keeps that way in for the night, so after that, just say which way they took. For each obstacle, read its box, then the roll line, then the line for the result. For a Cost, Trouble or anything else the dice do, turn to When It Happens. Each Success line is for the quiet way; if they took the loud way, read its own line if it has one. If a power opened a way of its own, describe how it went in your own words. On a later arrival, leave out anything already taken.

Other ideas. The roll line gives the usual ways past, but players can try any trait if they say how it gets them past, like Brawn to throw a goose or Charm to talk to the geese. You decide how it fits. A good fit: roll it at the obstacle’s Difficulty. Loud (noise, damage or a scene): it’s the loud way, Suspicion +1 whatever the result. A stretch: the Difficulty is 2 higher, unless a power is letting them roll that trait (like the Creature’s Brute Force). At a watched obstacle, Trouble still gets them caught.

The cask of red wine (essential) · food and drink, so the Cook’s trait die is one size bigger here · nothing here is watched, so no Tell check and nobody gets caught here.

The Grinning Turnip is the loudest place in Hallowby tonight, full of fiddle music and singing, with a line out the door. Nobody is paying any attention to the back.

Behind the tavern, a muddy yard full of geese leads to the kitchen door. In the alley beside it, a heavy trapdoor opens down into the cellar. Which way?

Way in · The goose yard

The yard is ankle-deep in mud and full of geese, and they start honking the moment a stranger gets close.

Roll Sly to tiptoe through, or Nimble to run straight through the flock (the loud way). Difficulty 6, not watched.

Success: You make it across the yard without a single honk. The kitchen door is unlocked, and the cellar stairs are just inside.

Success, the loud way: Geese scatter, feathers fly and the whole yard starts honking, but you make it inside.

Trouble: One goose spots you and starts honking, and the whole flock joins in. You back out of the yard, covered in mud. (Suspicion +1. Nobody is watching, so no chase.)

or Way in · The cellar trapdoor

In the alley there’s an oak trapdoor with iron bands, as heavy as a coffin lid.

Roll Brawn to heave it open. Difficulty 8, not watched.

Success: It lifts with a groan nobody hears over the fiddles. Steps lead down into the dark.

Trouble: It won’t budge, and all the scraping and banging draws looks from the street. (Suspicion +1. No chase.)

Then · The back room

The cellar is one dark, cluttered back room, full of barrels, sacks and forty years of things nobody threw away. The wine is in here somewhere.

Roll Wits to figure out which barrel it is, or Sly to rummage through everything (the loud way). Difficulty 8, not watched.

Success: Behind a row of pickle jars, you find a small cask with a faded red label.

Trouble: You knock over a shelf of pots and pans. Upstairs, the music stops for a long moment before it starts up again. (Suspicion +1. No chase.)

Whoever got past the back room is holding the cask of red wine, and the essential is yours.

Mark the wine on the tracker, with who carries it.

The pot of nightshade · plants and seeds, so the Gardener’s trait die is one size bigger here · watched, so the first time anyone arrives, make a Tell check once everyone moving here this Turn has arrived (When It Happens).

Mrs. Thorne, the florist, is selling festival garlands as fast as she can wrap them. Her shop is packed with people in costume, and from behind the counter she can see every one of them.

The nightshade sits on a high shelf at the back. Up the side wall, a rickety drainpipe runs to an open window just above that shelf. Which way?

Way in · The crowded shop group · watched

The shop is packed with witches, skeletons and a man in a bear suit, all in line for garlands.

Roll Sly to slip through the crowd. Difficulty 8, watched. It’s a crowd, so each of you who wants to get past rolls separately. Whoever gets through takes the pot, and if several get through at once, you choose who.

Success: You work your way through the crowd, saying “excuse me” a lot, and the nightshade is in your hands.

Trouble: Someone steps on your foot, and you yelp in a voice that isn’t quite human. The whole shop turns around, and someone shouts, “Thief!” (Suspicion +1, and caught in a local chase.)

If two or more roll the crowd in the same Turn, that’s a group check (When It Happens). A Ghost with its Spectral Perk isn’t stopped by the crowd, because it’s a group way in. It walks through with no roll and no action, even in the Turn it arrives, and takes the pot (unless it’s already carrying something).

or Way in · The drainpipe

The alley beside the shop is empty, and the drainpipe is held to the wall by three rusty brackets.

Roll Nimble to climb it. Difficulty 10, not watched.

Success: You climb up and in through the window, and the nightshade is right there on the shelf.

Trouble: The drainpipe pulls away from the wall with you still on it, and you fall into the alley with a crash. (Suspicion +1. No chase.)

Whoever got through has the pot of nightshade.

A set of new hinges · tools and hardware, so the Handyman’s trait die is one size bigger here · watched, with a Tell check on the first arrival.

The carpenter’s workshop is closed for the festival. The street outside is busy with families heading to the square, and every few minutes the night watchman walks past with his lantern.

The front door is locked. Around back, a high garden wall hides the lumberyard. Through the window you can see the hinges hanging on a board above the workbench. Which way?

Way in · The front door watched

The front door is solid and has a good lock, and it’s in full view of the street.

Roll Sly to pick the lock, or Brawn to kick it in (the loud way). Difficulty 8, watched.

Success: The lock clicks, and the door swings open without a sound.

Success, the loud way: One kick and the door bursts open, and you’re inside.

Trouble: The lock holds, and a man walking by stops and asks what you think you’re doing. (Suspicion +1, and caught in a local chase.)

or Way in · The garden wall

The garden wall is high brick with broken glass along the top, and its gate is padlocked.

Roll Nimble to climb it, or Brawn to break through the gate (the loud way). Difficulty 8, not watched.

Success: You drop over the wall between the stacks of lumber, and the back door isn’t even locked.

Success, the loud way: The gate crashes down, lock and all, and you’re in among the stacks of lumber.

Trouble: Halfway up, the top of the wall comes away in your hands. (Suspicion +1. No chase.)

Trouble, the loud way: The gate doesn’t budge. (Suspicion +1. No chase.)

Then · The night watchman watched

You’re inside, but the workbench is under the front window, and here comes the watchman again.

Roll Wits to time his rounds. Difficulty 8, watched.

Success: You wait for his lantern to swing away and grab the hinges. When he looks in again, the room is empty.

Trouble: He comes back early, and his lantern swings right onto you. “Hey! You there!” (Suspicion +1, and caught in a local chase.)

Whoever got past the watchman has the hinges.

A new cape · cloth and costumes, so the Tailor’s trait die is one size bigger here, the guard dog included · watched, with a Tell check on the first arrival · the mirror is here.

The tailor’s shop is brightly lit. Mrs. Pinch, the tailor, stands behind her counter with a mouthful of pins, and the children judging the costume contest will be here any minute.

The new cape hangs on a stand behind her, and the side window is shuttered. At the back of the shop, next to a tall gold-framed mirror, a huge dog is asleep. Which way?

Way in · Mrs. Pinch at the counter watched

Mrs. Pinch looks you up and down and takes the pins out of her mouth.

Roll Charm to talk her into it, or Sly to snatch it from under her nose (the loud way). Difficulty 8, watched.

Success: You tell her it’s for the costume contest, and she’s so pleased that she wraps it up for you.

Success, the loud way: You grab the cape and you’re gone before the pins hit the floor.

Trouble: She looks at you over her glasses, and her face goes pale. “That’s not a costume,” she says, and then she screams. (Suspicion +1, and caught in a local chase.)

or Way in · The shuttered window

The side window is in a dark alley, and its shutters are latched from the inside.

Roll Nimble to lift the latch and climb in, or Brawn to force the shutters (the loud way). Difficulty 10, not watched.

Success: You lift the latch with a fingernail and climb in, and soon the cape is over your arm.

Success, the loud way: The shutters give with a bang, and you’re in.

Trouble: The shutter swings back and bangs like a gunshot, and Mrs. Pinch drops her pins. (Suspicion +1, but no chase, because nobody saw who.)

Whoever got in has the new cape.

The Mirror

Once the cape has been taken, anyone at the tailor’s may try for the mirror (if the way in was a way only one of them could take, only that one). Taking it, once they’re past the dog, is free. Before anyone takes it, count aloud. From the Turn it’s taken, it adds Suspicion +1 at the end of every Turn until it leaves town, usually 2 in all if it goes straight to the bridge, so warn them if it would reach the Limit.

Then · The guard dog watched · for the mirror

The dog is the size of a small pony, and it’s lying across the foot of the mirror. As you watch, one of its eyes opens.

Roll Charm to win it over with a treat and a pat, or Nimble to outrun it while it barks (the loud way). Difficulty 10 (it’s guarding the furniture), watched.

Success: The dog thumps its tail twice, rolls over and lets you take the mirror.

Success, the loud way: You run past with the dog at your heels, and by the time it skids to a stop, the mirror is yours.

Trouble: The dog jumps up and barks loud enough to wake the whole street. (Suspicion +1, and caught in a local chase.)

Read this when someone takes the mirror. If it’s the Creature, leave out “your Nimble is one size smaller”: its Tireless Perk keeps its Nimble the same size.

The mirror is Bulky, which means one of you can carry it. While you do, you can’t use the Mask, your Nimble is one size smaller, and every move takes your action in two Turns in a row. After the first you’re somewhere in between, and you arrive when you act in the second.

A mirror that size also gets noticed. From now on, Suspicion goes up by 1 at the end of every Turn until it’s out of town. You can put it down any time, except when you’ve been caught and are running for it, but setting it down doesn’t stop the Suspicion. Only giving it up for good does that.

If Dracula is in the shop, the mirror shows the counter, the dog and everybody except him (flavor only). Taking the mirror back up after it’s set down is an action. Abandoned, it stays where it is, makes no more noise, and can’t be taken again.

Always watched. The first time anyone arrives who isn’t a captive, make a Tell check. A captive’s arrival doesn’t count. For rescue and slipping free, see When It Happens.

The lock-up is a small stone building behind the square, with one barred door and one barred window. The constable is asleep in a chair outside with his hat over his eyes.

Always watched. The first time anyone comes back here, make a Tell check. Only when everyone who isn’t locked up is here may one of them roll.

The stone bridge is at the edge of town. Families with lanterns are crossing it on their way home, and beyond it the path climbs through the woods to the castle.

If anyone is in the lock-up, read this before anyone rolls.

Anyone still in the lock-up when you cross is left behind. Are you sure you’re all here?

The way out watched

One of you rolls for everybody: Sly to slip across with the crowd, Nimble to go along under the bridge, or Brawn to barge straight through (the loud way). Difficulty 6, watched.

Success or Cost: You’re across, and the woods close behind you. (The Cost here costs nothing. Even if this roll takes Suspicion to the Limit, they’re out, and nobody runs. Turn to Part Three.)

Trouble: A man holds his lantern up to your face and screams. (Suspicion +1, and the roller is caught in a local chase. The way out can be rolled only once a Turn, so the party tries again next Turn.)

A Cost

The roller does it, but you pick one cost. Never pick one that costs nothing right then, such as Suspicion +1 on a roll, or a group check, that already raised it (an overdraw’s +2 doesn’t count here, since it goes on top), “drop an item” from someone carrying nothing, or a lost Turn when nothing is waiting, or a smaller die when the roller’s next roll is a d12 at its own Duty’s place (the bigger die cancels it).

Read the line aloud
Suspicion +1You do it, but somebody noticed something strange about you. Suspicion goes up by 1.
Drop an itemYou do it, but in the scramble you drop something. It’s lying right here.
Lose a TurnYou do it, but it takes a long time, and you miss your next Turn.
Smaller dieYou do it, but you’ve twisted something. Your next roll’s trait die is one size smaller.

Drop an item: one item of loot the roller carries, which you pick, though never what this roll wins and never the mirror. It stays in this place, and picking up dropped items is an action. Mix up the Costs. A dropped item works well, because someone has to come back for it.

A lost Turn still owed when the final flight starts is forgotten.

Trouble

It doesn’t happen, and Suspicion +1. Read the obstacle’s Trouble line. If the obstacle is watched, the roller is caught, so turn to Caught. If not, that’s all, and they can try again next Turn. One Perk changes this. The Invisible Man (Out of Sight) isn’t caught unless he, or anyone where he is, carries loot or the mirror (Suspicion still +1).

The Monster Shows

When the Monster d10 rolls higher than the trait die, Suspicion +2, whatever the result. Not on a tie, and never with the Mask. If an ability let them roll the Monster without risking Suspicion (the Werewolf’s Good Dog, the Invisible Man’s Unseen, some Gifts), its showing adds nothing. One Perk changes this, Dracula’s Hypnotic Eyes, on his Charm rolls. When the Monster shows on one of Jekyll’s rolls, the roll stands, and then Hyde takes over, free, even if an ability meant it added nothing. In a chase, a show counts toward the chase’s one rise instead (Caught).

Read the line aloud
DraculaHis shadow stretches the wrong way across the street, and it has wings.
The CreatureIt straightens to its full height, and the stitches across its face show in the lantern light.
The MummyA bandage comes loose and keeps unwinding, and there’s nobody inside it.
The WerewolfFur bristles across its face and hands, and its teeth grow long and sharp.
The Invisible ManA glove slips off, and there’s no hand inside it.
A GhostIt flickers, and for a moment the wall behind it shows through.
A WitchGreen sparks crackle off her fingertips, and every lantern in the street flares.
Jekyll & HydeThe kindly doctor’s face twists into somebody else’s.

A Critical

A Success where both dice show the same number. Outside a chase, the roller gets back one charge it spent (never more than 3), so read the box. In a chase it counts as two Successes, and you say instead, “You leave them far behind.”

That was perfect, as clean as anything you’ve ever done. If you’ve spent a charge tonight, you get one back.

A Tell Check

Make one the first time anyone reaches a watched place, which means the florist, the carpenter, the tailor, the lock-up (not a captive’s arrival) and the way out once anyone comes back to it. Each place is checked once a night. Wait until everyone moving there this Turn has arrived (if you’re not sure who else is coming, ask), then roll a d6. On 4–6, a Tell goes off. Number the arrivals and roll a d6 to pick one (for two arrivals, 1–3 is the first and 4–6 the second; for three, 1–2, 3–4, 5–6; for more, reroll a number nobody has), and read its line. Suspicion +1, and that’s its only effect. The Witch’s Familiar’s Warning: if she is among the arrivals, a Tell goes off only if a second d6 also rolls 4–6.

Read the line aloud
DraculaA dark store window reflects the whole street, with its lanterns, its crowd and its carved turnips, and everyone in it but you. Someone looks from the window to you and back again.
The CreatureYou stand a head above the whole crowd, and no costume in the world hides it. A child on her father’s shoulders looks you right in the eye.
The MummyYou leave a trail of dust behind you, and a smell of old spices. A woman sniffs, frowns and follows the trail with her eyes, all the way to you.
The WerewolfYour eyebrows meet in the middle, and there’s too much hair everywhere else. A man nudges his friend, and they both stare at you a little too long.
The Invisible ManYou sneeze, and everyone nearby turns to look. Behind your bandages, goggles and false nose, they can see there’s no face at all.
A GhostThe candles flicker as you drift in, and everyone’s breath fogs. Someone pulls their coat tighter and looks around for where the cold is coming from.
A WitchYour black cat sits down in the middle of the floor and stares at people without blinking, and one by one, they stare back.
Jekyll & HydeOne of your hands is a gentleman’s, and the other is hairy and knotted. The man who just shook it pulls his hand back and stares.

A Group Check

When two or more roll the florist’s crowded shop in the same Turn. Everyone declares their trait, their die and any charges first, then all roll at once. Each gets past on its own result. Suspicion rises only once for the whole check, by the biggest single trigger among the rolls. Everyone who gets Trouble is caught together, and flees together on one Lead (Caught, below).

You go into the crowd together. Ready? Everybody roll at once.

Caught: the Local Chase

Trouble at a watched obstacle. If that Trouble takes Suspicion to the Limit, there’s no local chase: turn to The Final Flight, where the runner flees with everyone else. The whole chase, however many rounds, happens inside this Turn. While it lasts, the runner can’t drop, abandon or hand over anything. With the Werewolf’s Night Runner, fleeing alone when the chase starts, say the Lead starts at 2.

They’ve seen you. Somebody shouts, and somebody else grabs a broom. Run!

This is a chase. Your Lead starts at 1. Get it to 4 and you’ve lost them. If it drops to 0, they’ve cornered you. Every round, I’ll tell you what the ground is like, and it gives you two traits to choose from. Roll one of them, with the Mask or the Monster, against the mob. Any ability of yours can make your die one size bigger instead, even one your card says never works in a chase, but nobody else can spend a charge on your roll. A Success puts your Lead up by 1, Trouble puts it down by 1, and a Cost leaves it where it is. After six rounds it’s over: with a Lead of 2 or more you get away, and with anything less they’ve got you.

Suspicion doesn’t move until the chase is over. Then it goes up once: by 2 if your Monster showed at any point, or else by 1 if you had any Trouble in the chase, and not at all if neither happened. At the start of any round, before anyone rolls, you can give up and let them take you, and everything you carry, to the lock-up.

  1. The Lead starts at 1. With the Werewolf’s Night Runner, fleeing alone when the chase starts, it starts at 2.
  2. The mob’s Difficulty is 8 plus half the Suspicion, rounded down, at most 11, worked out when the chase starts (after the rise from the roll that got them caught). It stays the same for the whole chase. Suspicion 0–1: 8 · 2–3: 9 · 4–5: 10 · 6–8: 11. With the Mummy’s Fear the Curse, if it flees alone when the chase starts, 1 lower.
  3. Each round, roll a d6 on the ground table below and read the line. The runner picks one of its two traits, and the Mask or the Monster (carrying the mirror: no Mask, and Nimble one size smaller, though not the Creature’s). Abilities go on the runner’s own roll only, with nobody else’s charges, and any may be spent as a raise instead. No Castle Duty in a chase.
  4. Move the Lead: a Success +1 (a Critical +2), a Cost no change, Trouble −1.
  5. One chase, one rise. Note the biggest trigger among the chase’s rolls (Trouble +1, the Monster showing +2). When the chase ends, add it to Suspicion, with +2 more for each overdraw (one per runner).
  6. The Weakness: from round 1 for Dracula and a Ghost, from round 3 for everyone else, the runner’s trait die is one size smaller to the end of the chase. Read its line when it starts. A bigger die from an ability cancels it for that roll.
  7. Escape at 4 puts them back where they were caught, with this Turn used up. Cornered at 0, they’re captured (below). After round 6, a Lead of 2 or more escapes, and less is cornered. A runner may also give up at the start of any round, once the ground is read and before anyone rolls: captured, no roll. A chase given up before anyone has rolled raises nothing.
  8. If the rise brings Suspicion to the Limit, turn to The Final Flight once the chase is settled. A runner who escaped joins the flight; anyone cornered, or who gave up, is in the lock-up and stays there. If that leaves nobody outside the lock-up, nobody runs. Turn to Part Three, where the year is Forked.

Caught together. When several get Trouble in the same group check, they’re caught together. Each of them rolls each round, in any order they like, and the Lead moves once for the round by the majority rule (The Final Flight). The chase still rises once, when it ends, by the biggest trigger among all their rolls. Anyone may give up at the start of a round, and the rest carry on. A Perk that changes a local chase only works for someone fleeing alone when the chase starts, so another runner giving up later doesn’t bring it in.

The Ground (d6, every round of any chase)

1The crowded squareLose yourself in the crowd, or bluff your way through. Sly, Charm.
2Back alleysDodge around corners and double back. Nimble, Sly.
3The market stallsTip over a cart or jump over a stall. Brawn, Nimble.
4Over the rooftopsClimb up, jump across and find a way down. Nimble, Wits.
5The festival paradeJoin the parade and blend in with the costumes. Charm, Sly.
6A dead endBreak through, or think of another way out. Brawn, Wits.

The Mob Brings Your Weakness

Read the line aloud
Dracula: GarlicRound 1Someone at the front is waving a string of garlic like a lantern.
The Creature: FireRound 3Someone has lit torches, and the flames are coming closer.
The Mummy: A Loose ThreadRound 3A small boy has grabbed a loose end, and he won’t let go.
The Werewolf: HoundsRound 3Behind the mob, someone has let the hunting dogs out.
The Invisible Man: FlourRound 3A bag of flour bursts all over you, and now everyone can see you.
A Ghost: Cold IronRound 1Suddenly the street is full of cold iron: horseshoes, railings and a fire poker someone brought from home.
A Witch: RowanRound 3Old Granny Mott has a sprig of rowan, and she’s holding it up at you.
Jekyll & Hyde: A Familiar FaceRound 3“Doctor Jekyll? Is that you?”

Captured

Cornered in a local chase, or gave up. The town takes back everything the captive carried, the mirror included. All of it is gone for the night, and nobody can take any of it again. Put the captive’s token in the lock-up.

Hands grab you from every side and pin you to the ground. When you catch your breath, you’re in the lock-up, and everything you were carrying is gone.

If this chase’s rise brought Suspicion to the Limit, stop here: nobody can slip free or come back for the captive now. If every Entity is now in the lock-up, the night is over; turn to Part Three, where the year is Forked. Otherwise, read on.

Starting next Turn, you can try to slip free once a Turn, or the others can come and get you. Anyone still in here when they leave town is left behind.

A captive can’t pick anything up or be handed anything, but can still spend charges on any roll at the lock-up, whether its own, a rescuer’s or another captive’s.

Rescue and Slipping Free

A rescue watched

Anyone not held, at the lock-up (getting there is a move), rolls Sly to sneak past the constable, or Brawn to tear the door off (the loud way). Difficulty 10, watched.

Success or Cost: every captive there is free (pick a Cost as usual). The freed act again next Turn, from the lock-up. If this roll’s Suspicion reaches the Limit, they’re still free, and they join the final flight.

The way is clear, and the constable keeps snoring.

Trouble: Suspicion +1, and the rescuer is caught in a local chase.

The constable’s hat slips off, and he’s wide awake.

Slipping free watched

The captive rolls once a Turn, from the Turn after its capture: Sly or Nimble, or Brawn (the loud way). Difficulty 10, watched.

Success: free, and acts again next Turn, from the lock-up. If this roll’s Suspicion reaches the Limit, it’s still free, and it joins the final flight. A Cost: nothing happens. Trouble: Suspicion +1, but no chase.

You work the door open and slip out into the night.

The lock-up is watched, so Dracula’s Mesmerize works on both. A captive may also slip free by a way of its own (its card’s ability, at a Difficulty 2 lower). A rescue frees only those held at that moment.

Dropping, Picking Up and Handing Over

An Entity may drop its own loot, or the mirror it carries, any time, free, except while it’s caught (until its chase ends). Dropped things stay in that place; dropped between places, they stay at the place it left, and an Entity that sets the mirror down there is back at that place too. Anyone there may pick up any number of dropped items, as their action for a Turn. Loot can be handed to anyone in the same place, free, any time, though not while caught, and never to a captive.

Suspicion Rising

Flavor only. Read each line the first time Suspicion reaches or passes that number, so the players feel the town waking up. At the Limit, skip them and turn to The Final Flight. With five players (Limit 8), read each line at the number in parentheses.

Read the line aloud
3 (2)Somewhere a dog starts barking and doesn’t stop.
5 (4)The church bell starts ringing, even though it isn’t on the hour. In the square, someone says loudly, “Those aren’t costumes.”
7 (6)People are bringing pitchforks out of their sheds, and they aren’t for the parade anymore.
8 (7)People with lanterns are gathering in the square. One more thing, and they’ll come for you.

Overdraw

At zero charges an Entity can still use an ability, paying Suspicion +2 instead, on top of the roll’s other rise (in a local chase, on top of the chase’s one rise, and only once a chase). In the final flight it costs a smaller trait die instead (The Final Flight).

The End of a Turn, and Dawn

At the end of every Turn, if the mirror has been taken and is still in town (carried or set down, not lost or abandoned), Suspicion +1. Then move the Turn marker.

Read the line aloud
Start of Turn 10The sky over the woods is turning gray, and the music in the square is slowing down.
Start of Turn 12This is the last Turn before dawn, and the first birds are singing. Anyone still in town when the sun comes up will have to run for it.
End of Turn 12The sun comes up over Hallowby, and everyone in the street takes off their masks. You can’t take off yours.

After the end of Turn 12, everyone still in town who isn’t locked up goes to The Final Flight. If every Entity is in the lock-up at once, the night ends there. Turn to Part Three: the year is Forked.

When Suspicion reaches the Limit, or dawn comes with anyone still in town. Stop wherever you are, even in the middle of a Turn. If it was a local chase’s rise that brought it, anyone who escaped that chase runs too, and anyone cornered in it, or who gave up, is in the lock-up. Captives stay in the lock-up. If every Entity is in the lock-up, nobody runs. Turn to Part Three, where the year is Forked.

Hallowby has had enough. The bells are ringing, the music has stopped, and every lantern in town is turning toward you. The whole town is coming after you with pitchforks and brooms, and old Granny Mott is at the front.

Run for the castle, all of you, together, right now.

This is the final flight. Everyone who isn’t locked up runs together, from wherever you are.

Your Lead starts at 2. Get it to 5 and you’re home. If it drops to 0, they’ve got you, and you’re forked.

The masks are off now. Everyone rolls the Monster, and Suspicion doesn’t matter anymore. Every round I roll the ground, and it gives you two traits to choose from. Each of you rolls one of them against the mob, and you can spend charges on each other’s rolls. Any ability can now be spent just to make someone’s trait die one size bigger, whatever it usually does, even if your card says it never works in a chase.

Then we count. If you have more Successes than Trouble, your Lead goes up by 1, or by 2 if you’re two or more ahead. If you have more Trouble than Successes, it goes down the same way. If they’re tied, it stays the same. A Cost counts for neither, and a Critical counts as two Successes.

Anything you drop now stays in Hallowby.

Running It

  1. Who runs: every Entity who isn’t captured. The Lead starts at 2. Escape at 5. Cornered at 0 means Forked.
  2. The mob’s Difficulty is 10, however many run. Suspicion has stopped, and nothing raises it now.
  3. Each round: roll a d6 on the ground table (When It Happens) and read its line. Each runner picks one of its two traits. The Monster d10 only. Carrying the mirror makes Nimble one size smaller (not the Creature’s: it’s Tireless). Abilities may go on anyone’s roll, and any ability may be spent as a raise instead of doing what it usually does (one raise per roll). Everyone rolls, in any order the party likes.
  4. The majority rule: count the Successes (a Critical counts as two) and the Trouble; Costs count for neither. If Successes are ahead by 1, the Lead goes up 1, and by 2 or more, it goes up 2. If Trouble is ahead, it goes down the same way. A tie means no change. For example, a Success, a Critical, a Cost and a Trouble make 3 Successes to 1 Trouble, so the Lead goes up 2.
  5. The Weakness: the flight is a new chase for everyone, even someone who came straight from a local chase. From round 1 for Dracula and a Ghost, from round 3 for everyone else, the trait die is one size smaller to the end of the flight. Read its line. A bigger die from an ability cancels it for that roll.
  6. Overdraw now costs a smaller die instead of Suspicion. From the overdrawer’s own next roll to the end of the flight, its trait die is one size smaller, on top of any Weakness. Once per flight each, Weakness or not.

Home

The Lead reaches 5. Everyone in the flight is home, with everything they carry. Anyone still in the lock-up is left behind.

The last pitchfork falls behind in the woods, and the castle door slams shut behind you. Far below, you can still hear the town shouting.

You made it. Let’s see what you brought home.

Turn to Part Three.

Forked

The Lead reaches 0. The year’s result is Forked, whatever the party carries. Turn to Part Three and read only the Forked line.

They’ve cornered you at the bottom of the hill, with the castle’s windows glowing just above the trees. The lanterns close in, and the pitchforks come up.

You got forked.

pages.name: Part Three: How the Year Went

text.content:
About 5–10 minutes. An item, or the mirror, is home if an Entity who got out of town carries it, whether that Entity left by the way out or escaped the final flight. Find the result, then read its line.

Read the result’s line aloud
Grand YearA Win, and the mirror came home too.A year of plenty, and the new piece takes pride of place in the great hall.
WinThe wine came home, and no more than one of the other three items is missing.The pantry is full and the fires stay lit all year.
PartialNot a Win, but at least 2 of the 4 items came home. Without the wine, a Partial at best.The castle gets by, but barely, and the tower stays cold all winter.
Bust0 or 1 of the 4 items came home.A long, hard year, with too little to go around.
ForkedCornered in the final flight, or every Entity in the lock-up at once.The town tells the story for years, and next Lantern Night it keeps a closer watch.

Left behind: work out the result first, then drop it one step for each Entity left in the lock-up, so a Grand Year becomes a Win, a Win a Partial, a Partial a Bust. It never drops below Bust.

Then, unless the result is Forked, read one line for each item that didn’t come home. If the nightshade didn’t come home, or the year is Forked, leave out the part about the florist.

Read the line aloud
The wine (food and drink)Turnip soup every night until spring.
The nightshade (plants and seeds)Nothing grows in the garden but nettles.
The hinges (tools and hardware)Doors stick, hinges break and nothing gets fixed.
The cape (cloth and costumes)Next year’s disguises are old and patched together with string.

Goodnight

And that was Lantern Night in Hallowby. Down the hill, the town is waking up to find things missing, and the florist is wondering where her nightshade went.

Happy Halloween.

If your group wants more, the rulebook has three more towns and tables for rolling your own.
